title: add jsonschema strict mode with enhanced error reporting (OpenAI compat)
author: Anika Patel
description:
Summary: Add a strict JSON Schema response_format mode with improved validation and error messages for OpenAI compatibility. Motivation: customers using structured outputs need deterministic, machine-parseable responses and clear diagnostics when model outputs deviate. This PR implements: 1) response_format.type="json_schema" with strict=true option that enforces schema conformance at the API layer; 2) deterministic post-processing that extracts JSON from streaming tokens without blocking regular streaming behavior; 3) structured error payloads (error_code, path, expected, received, hint) surfaced in the API error response and included in logs for downstream evals; 4) enhanced OpenAI compatibility: the response follows the OpenAI-style response_format shape while retaining Redwood metadata (model_variant, topology); 5) docs, end-to-end tests, and migration notes.

Details: Implementation touches the response_format parser, the streaming assembler, and the schema validator. The validator uses a fast-path for common schema patterns (required/enum/type/objects) and falls back to full validation for complex constraints. In strict mode validation failures cause a 400 with a structured JSON error payload and the original model output attached (truncated). Non-strict mode will return a warning header and include a structured validation report in the response metadata. Streaming: the streaming assembler buffers minimal state to find the first valid JSON substring that matches the schema; it does not hold the full response to preserve low latency. Edge cases handled: nested arrays, trailing text after JSON, partial JSON across tokens, and multi-JSON outputs.

Checklist:
- [x] response_format parsing and API surface
- [x] strict validator implementation and unit tests
- [x] streaming extraction and integration tests
- [x] OpenAI compatibility layer mapping
- [x] docs and migration guide
- [x] examples in SDKs (Python/TS)

Compatibility & rollout: Default is strict=false to avoid breaking existing users. New API users can opt-in with response_format: { type: "json_schema", strict: true, schema: ... }. For Dedicated/Private deployments the feature is behind a runtime flag and will be included in the next minor release.

Why this change: reduces flakiness of downstream parsers, improves automated eval and regression detection, and gives clear actionable errors to prompt engineers and platform operators.
commits: feat(api): add json_schema response_format parsing and strict flag
feat(runtime): streaming assembler extract-json fast-path and minimal buffering
feat(validator): fast-path schema validator + structured error payloads
fix(tests): add integration tests for multi-token json and trailing text
docs: structured-output migration guide and examples
chore(sdk): examples for python and typescript clients
review_comments: Diego Ramirez: Great direction. A couple of thoughts: 1) can we avoid a full JSON parse on every token for streaming? 2) error_codes need to be stable (documented).
Anika Patel: Answered both — added a fast-path incremental extractor and documented the error_code enum in docs. See jsonschema_validator.ts for fast-path implementation.
Lena Cho: Please add a note about behavior for multiple top-level JSON objects in the response (we currently accept only the first matching JSON for strict mode).

Anika Patel: Added integration test and explicit behavior documented in migration guide — first matching JSON is used; if multiple valid matches exist we return the first and include a validation_event log with potential ambiguity.
Tom Barlow: Minor: adjust telemetry tag to include "jsonschema.strict" so we can signal-rollout by customer. Also confirm the added CPU overhead in CI perf job.
Anika Patel: Added telemetry tag and perf regression micro-benchmark. No measurable >5% CPU increase for typical schemas; documented tradeoffs in release notes.
merge_commit_message: Add jsonschema strict mode with enhanced error reporting (OpenAI compat) — squash merge
release_notes: Add opt-in JSON Schema strict mode for structured responses. Strict mode returns structured validation errors (error_code, path, expected, received, hint) and enforces machine-parseable outputs. Default is non-breaking (strict=false).
notes_for_ops: Feature behind runtime flag for Dedicated/Private. Watch validation_events and cpu/latency in initial rollout. Telemetry tag: jsonschema.strict. If customers experience high validation load, disable strict per-route or use sampling.
examples: TS: client.responses.create({ response_format: { type: 'json_schema', strict: true, schema: {...} } })
